sections.title: Boundary (security model, report §5)
comment: Attestations are things the repo cannot show; a human commits them under H6.

keys.name: autonomy_level
doc: L0 | L1 | L2 | L3 | L4 | L5   (report §6.2). The level you ask for; the doctor prints the
EFFECTIVE level, which is lower whenever a prerequisite or cap fails. Run
`python3 .claude/scripts/doctor.py --level` to see each cap and its reason.
L0 assist | L1 supervised local loop (today's V1) | L2 push-branch | L3 draft-PR factory
L4 async factory | L5 low-risk auto-merge. L4 and L5 need docs/baseline/evidence.json.

keys.name: github_repo
doc: owner/name of the GitHub repo the doctor reads rulesets from. Empty = derive from `origin`.

keys.name: bot.kind
doc: none | github-app | machine-user-pat   (report §5.1 B1). The identity the agent pushes as.
github-app        required at L3+
machine-user-pat  acceptable at L2 only, a fine-grained PAT that expires within 14 days
never a PAT that belongs to a human

keys.name: bot.login
doc: the bot's GitHub login (for an App, `<slug>[bot]`). Never a human's login.

keys.name: bot.id
doc: numeric id of the App or machine user, as it would appear in a ruleset's bypass_actors.

keys.name: bot.token_expires
doc: machine-user-pat only: the PAT's expiry date, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be at most 14 days away.

keys.name: solo_maintainer
doc: true on a one-human install. The human admin may then bypass rulesets in pull_request mode
only (RC-9); the bot never may. false (default) means no bypass actors at all.

keys.name: deploy_triggers
doc: HUMAN ATTESTATION (report §8.4, B5): every workflow that deploys, found by the doctor or declared.
- workflow: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
fires_on: "push:main"            # push:main | push:branches | tag | release | workflow_run | ...
gate: gated-by-environment       # or: none
A deploy on a bot-pushable ref with gate none caps the level at L1; on main, at L4.

keys.name: git_integrated_hosts
doc: HUMAN ATTESTATION: hosts that deploy from git with no workflow in the repo (dashboard config).
- host: vercel
previews_on: none               # none | label | all-branches | pull-requests
production_on: main
gate: none                      # none | gated-by-environment | manual

keys.name: deploy_surface.attested_at
doc: date (YYYY-MM-DD) the human last attested deploy_triggers and git_integrated_hosts.

keys.name: deploy_surface.fingerprint
doc: sha256 printed by `doctor --deploy-surface`. A change to any deploy-surface file makes it stale
and the attestation void until a human re-attests (report §8.4).

keys.name: sandbox_verified
doc: date (YYYY-MM-DD) the human confirmed the OS sandbox really is active (V19). Empty = unverified,
which keeps the level at L1.

keys.name: agent_isolation
doc: none | separate-os-user | devcontainer | container   (report §5.1 B3). What the human attests
keeps the agent away from their credentials. A devcontainer or container with no credentials
also satisfies the managed-settings requirement at L3.

keys.name: managed_settings_verified
doc: date (YYYY-MM-DD) managed settings (allowManagedHooksOnly, disableBypassPermissionsMode) were
installed for the OS user that runs the loop. Needed at L3+ unless agent_isolation is a container.

keys.name: platform_attested
doc: GitHub features the human confirmed are available on this repo's plan, for what the doctor
cannot read (report section 8.4, V27). Unknown means unavailable. Names: rulesets,
code_owner_review, required_status_checks, bot_no_bypass, environment_reviewers,
apply_human_dispatch (IaC apply only by a human-started workflow), g3_ci_only (held-out
tests run only in CI, RC-6), push_rulesets.

keys.name: factory_approvers
doc: logins of the humans whose labels count (`factory:go`, `plan-ok`, `preview`). The label-guard
workflow template removes the label when anyone else applies it (RC-20).

keys.name: promotion_attested
doc: date (YYYY-MM-DD) the human confirmed the §6.3 promotion bar is met. Needed for L5.

keys.name: mcp_allowed_servers
doc: names of MCP servers or plugins the human accepts in a loop run (report section 5.6), for
example a read-only docs server. Any other deploy-capable server caps the level at L1.
